overview: Branch Cash Replenishment Optimisation addresses resource allocation is planned in silos, producing avoidable delays and occasionally infeasible instructions in banking and payments operations. The first proof of value uses ATM withdrawals, branch demand and CIT schedules. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is idle cash and cash-out hours, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: ATM withdrawals, branch demand and CIT schedules; define idle cash and cash-out hours and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Head of Payments / Chief Risk Officer.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including replay disruption and edge cases with hard constraints enforced.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
